Last updated July 2026 — currently finishing my MSc dissertation at LSE, open to data science and analytics opportunities from September 2026.
I build data-driven tools and models that turn complex information into clearer insights. I’m completing an MSc in Data Science at the London School of Economics (graduating September 2026), where my dissertation develops an augmented Elo rating system for football match outcome prediction — combining a four-stage optimisation pipeline (backpropagation through time, ISTA, SAGA, cross-validation) to beat canonical Elo on out-of-sample log-loss. I hold a BSc in Computer Science and Statistics from St. Lawrence University.
My broader project work spans Bayesian inference on football league data, interactive Shiny applications for F1 telemetry, graph neural networks for urban mobility forecasting, and distributed ML pipelines on GCP — hands-on experience across the full data science stack, from messy real-world data to deployed models.
I’m drawn to data science and analytics roles where I can work as part of a team to uncover patterns in real-world data and translate them into decisions that matter, with a particular interest in sports, betting, and motorsport analytics. Though, I am open to strong opportunities across industries. Outside of technical work, I’ve sharpened my ability to communicate ideas to different audiences through competitive swim coaching and academic mentoring, skills I can bring directly into a new team.
If anything here interests you, feel free to reach out!

title: Projects
text:
Augmented Elo Rating System for Football Match Outcome Prediction
MSc Capstone, The Ranking Room · London School of Economics · 2026


Python PyTorch Optimisation


Developed an augmented Elo rating system that learns team-strength adjustments directly from match data, extending the canonical Elo framework with a four-stage optimisation pipeline: backpropagation through time, ISTA for sparse feature selection, SAGA for stochastic optimisation, and cross-validation for model selection. Rating system is compareed against exisiting methods like Dixon-Coles and FIFA World Ranking, as well as market implied probabilites. Built as part of a three-person capstone partnered with the Trilemma Foundation.
therankingroom.substack.com




Tracking Team Strength: Bayesian Inference for Football League Standings
Bayesian Machine Learning · London School of Economics · 2026


Python Bayesian Inference Gibbs Sampling Kalman Filtering


Modelled evolving team strength across four seasons (2021–25) of FA Women’s Super League data using a Bayesian linear regression fit via Gibbs sampling and a Kalman filter for dynamic strength tracking. The Gibbs sampler achieved an RMSE of 1.440, narrowly outperforming OLS (1.441), while the Kalman filter reached 57.3% match outcome accuracy and correlated strongly (Spearman ~0.90–0.98) with actual league standings.




F1 Miami Grand Prix Lap Time Dataset — SCORE Network
Published Case Study · The SCORE Network · 2026


R Statistics Data Curation


Co-authored a published case study and dataset (1,138 rows of lap-by-lap timing data from the 2023 F1 Miami Grand Prix) for the SCORE Network’s sports data repository, a resource used in statistics classrooms for teaching summary statistics, distribution analysis, and outlier detection. Available publicly with citation.
Kuduk & Ramler (2026) · DOI · Dataset page




Predicting Flight Delay Severity at ORD, JFK & ATL
Distributed Computing for Big Data · 2026


Python Apache Spark MLlib Ensemble Learning GCP


Framed flight delay prediction as a four-class severity classification problem (no delay, minor, major, severe/cancellation) using five years of US Bureau of Transportation Statistics data covering ~3.5M flights across three major hub airports. Built and evaluated six model configurations in Apache Spark MLlib — logistic regression, decision tree, and KNN baselines alongside bagging, boosting, and a stacking ensemble — comparing both predictive performance and distributed scalability metrics such as training time, speedup ratio, and memory usage.




Predictive Forecasting of Citi Bike Station Demand in NYC
Distributed Computing for Big Data · 2026


Python Graph Attention Networks PyTorch Spatio-temporal


Developed a spatio-temporal graph attention network (MWI-DSTGAT) to forecast hourly bike inflow and outflow at 700+ NYC Citi Bike stations, supporting smarter rebalancing logistics and reducing empty or full-station scenarios. Constructed a spatial graph from station coordinates and flow patterns, incorporated NYC hourly weather data via a dedicated injection mechanism, and benchmarked against LSTM, GRU, and ARIMA baselines across ~30M trip records spanning 2013–2023. Implemented in PyTorch, departing transparently from the assignment’s TensorFlow specification.




F1 Popularity Growth & Sustainability Analysis
Managing and Visualising Data · 2025/2026


Python Pandas Plotly Seaborn REST APIs


Investigated the relationship between F1’s global popularity growth and its sustainability challenges across multiple decades of race calendar data. Integrated circuit location, attendance, and YouTube engagement data from the official F1 channel to explore how calendar expansion, track tenure, and travel intensity have evolved alongside fan demand. Analysed the impact of Drive to Survive on digital engagement trends and examined whether calendar geography has been optimised in line with F1’s net-zero-by-2030 commitment.




Interactive F1 Qualifying Analysis
Statistics SYE (Honors) - St. Lawrence University · 2024–2025


R Shiny Data Viz


Built an interactive Shiny application for exploring F1 telemetry and qualifying data across the 2018–2024 seasons. Users can compare two drivers head-to-head within a race or track a single driver’s performance over time through customizable, publication-quality visualizations.

AI-Augmented Physical Therapy App
Computer Science SYE (Honors) - St. Lawrence University · 2024–2025


Flutter PostgreSQL Docker


Developed a cross-platform app for athletes and individuals managing chronic injuries, featuring scheduling, calendar views, and a customizable exercise library. Designed a relational data model for exercises, routines, and user progress, backed by a PostgreSQL database in Docker. Leveraged AI-assisted development workflows (ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot) throughout the build.

title: Relevant Coursework
text:
Here is some information about relevant courses that I have taken at St. Lawrence.






NoteCS219 - Techniques of Computer Science





An in-depth look at computing and programming in a high-level language (Java). Introduces more advanced programming problems and more principled programming techniques.









NoteCS256 - Data Structures





An overview of the essential strategies for the organization, retrieval and processing of data. Topics include arrays, lists, stacks, queues, maps, and trees, as well as an introduction to algorithm analysis.









NoteCS220 - Computer Organization





An in-depth look at the underlying organization and architecture of modern computer systems. Topics include data representation, the organization of CPUs including caches and the memory hierarchy, digital circuits, machine language, and an introduction to C and assembly language programming.









NoteCS362 - Algorithm Analysis





An investigation of core techniques for designing and analyzing algorithms for computational problem-solving. Introduces well-known algorithms for common types of problems, and teaches students to evaluate algorithm efficiency.









NoteCS/DATA345 - Database Systems





A look at how data is logically organized, physically stored on a digital device, and queried. Focuses primarily on relational database systems and structured queries. Other topics include non-relational data models, privacy, security, performance, and reliability.









NoteCS/STAT345 - Statistical & Machine Learning





Introduces techniques for developing advanced models from datasets, for the purposes of better understanding the data and making predictions about future data. Techniques include linear and regularized regression, nearest neighbor classification, support vector machines, decision tree ensembles, and neural networks. Examines real-world applications, both successes and failures, the latter of which often involve data with embedded biases. Students will develop both technical and ethical competence in using some of the most powerful computational tools in data science.









NoteSTAT213 - Applied Regression Analysis





A continuation of Statistics 113 intended for students in the physical, social or behavioral sciences. Topics include simple and multiple linear regression, model diagnostics and testing, residual analysis, transformations, indicator variables, variable selection techniques, logistic regression, and analysis of variance. Most methods assume use of a statistical computing package.









NoteSTAT/DATA234 - Foundations of Data Science





An introduction to fundamental data science concepts using modern statistical programming languages and software. The course assumes no prior knowledge of programming but a familiarity with basic statistics is required. The course focuses on building essential data science skills such as data manipulation and visualization, basics of programming, string manipulation, and modern data sources (such as web and databases). Emphasis will be placed on building skills applicable to large scale projects.









NoteMATH280 - A Bridge to Higher Math





This course is designed to introduce students to the concepts and methods of higher mathematics. Techniques of mathematical proof are emphasized. Topics include logic, set theory, relations, functions, induction, cardinality, and others selected by the instructor.









NoteMATH205 - Multivariable Calculus





This course extends the fundamental concepts and applications of calculus, such as differentiation, integration, graphical analysis and optimization, to functions of several variables. Additional topics include the gradient vector, parametricequations and series.









NoteMATH217 - Linear Algebra





A study of finite dimensional linear spaces, systems of linear equations, matrices, determinants, bases, linear transformations, change of bases and eigen values.
